sections.h2: How can I sell my house fast in Buffalo, NY?
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell it yourself, or accept a cash offer from a buyer like us, and the cash route is the quickest because no lender has to approve the buyer. In Buffalo the choice often comes down to condition. A worn two-family with deferred repairs, or a rental that has not passed the city's inspection, is slow to sell on the open market but straightforward for an investor to price as-is.

Buffalo is a city of renters. The Census Bureau counts owners living in only 43.0% of homes for 2020-2024, so a large share of the housing stock is income property that has to meet city registration rules before it can legally earn rent. That shapes who buys here and what they look for in a house.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about housing in Buffalo?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 274,613 people lived in Buffalo on July 1, 2025, down 1.3% from the April 2020 estimates base. The figures below show why a repair bill can swallow a large share of a sale price here.

With a median home value of $164,200, a $25,000 roof or porch rebuild is a meaningful slice of what the house is worth. Sellers who carry that kind of work into a listing usually see it come back as a price cut.

sections.h2: Where is Buffalo and how did it become a city?
sections.html:
Buffalo sits on the eastern shore of Lake Erie at the head of the Niagara River and is the seat of Erie County. Wikipedia gives its area as 52.48 square miles, of which 40.38 is land and 12.10 is water.

The land around Buffalo Creek passed through the Holland Land Purchase, and Buffalo was chosen as the terminus of the Erie Canal in 1825. It incorporated as a city in 1832 and became a major grain port, then the second-largest railway hub in the country after Chicago, and later a steel town. Deindustrialization and the St. Lawrence Seaway pulled that economy apart, and the city has since leaned on health care, education, retail, logistics and tourism.

sections.h2: Which Buffalo neighborhoods and roads matter to a buyer?
sections.html:
Wikipedia notes that Buffalo's West Side is generally more affluent than its East Side, and that investment has gathered in a handful of districts since the 1990s. A house's address can move its value as much as its condition does.

  • Elmwood Village led the wave of reinvestment that began in the 1990s.
  • Larkinville grew out of the 2002 redevelopment of the Larkin Terminal Warehouse.
  • Downtown added more than 1,000 housing units between 2010 and 2017, and Seneca One Tower was redeveloped in 2020.
  • The Buffalo Niagara Medical Campus covers about 120 acres north of downtown.

I-190, NY 5 and NY 33 are the main expressways, and the Peace Bridge links I-190 to Canada. NFTA Metro Rail runs 6.4 miles from Canalside to the University Heights district. Buffalo Public Schools enroll roughly 34,000 students in about 60 schools, and the University at Buffalo, Buffalo State University, Canisius University and D'Youville University all operate in the city.

The city adopted its Green Code in 2017, replacing zoning rules more than sixty years old. If you plan a change of use, such as turning a house into a different number of units, ask City Hall which code district applies before you spend money.

sections.h2: How does a Buffalo winter affect the value of a house?
sections.html:
Buffalo has a humid continental climate, and lake-effect snow bands off Lake Erie define the winters. Wikipedia, citing Fox Weather, puts average snowfall near 95 inches a year and ranks Buffalo among the five snowiest large cities in the country.

Roofs, gutters, porches and plumbing take the abuse, so buyers walk those areas first. A seller who cannot afford to replace a worn roof before listing is a good candidate for an as-is sale, because an investor prices the roof into the offer and does not ask you to fix it.

sections.h2: What city rules apply if my Buffalo house is a rental?
sections.html:
The city's rental rules decide how easy a tenant-occupied house is to sell, so check them before you list.

  • Every non-owner-occupied one- or two-family house must be on the Rental Registry, whether or not it is occupied. Some three-family and mixed-use buildings are covered as well.
  • A new registration costs $100. Since January 1, 2025 the yearly fee has been $50 for a single unit and $100 for a two-unit house.
  • Registered properties are scheduled for proactive inspection and must hold a Certificate of Rental Compliance. A property that fails cannot operate as an income property, and the tenants cannot be evicted for unpaid rent.
  • Landlords certify that a house built before 1978 may contain lead hazards, and a Certificate of Occupancy is denied where a lead-paint hazard exists.
  • The city's Lead Hazard Reduction Grant offers up to $12,000 per unit in the Upper West Side and Schiller Park neighborhoods.

Short-term rentals need their own license. Any stay under six months counts, each address needs a separate license, it renews every year, and a new owner has to start the application over. Non-owner-occupied properties also need a special use permit. The Rental Registration office is at 65 Niagara Square, Room 304, phone 716-851-5621, and the short-term rental team answers at 716-851-4077.

sections.h2: What does closing cost in Erie County and who handles the deed?
sections.html:
The Erie County Clerk records the deed, and the clerk's page lists the charges that apply.

  • $45 statutory recording fee plus $5 for each written page
  • $10 to file the TP-584 transfer tax form
  • $125 to file the RP-5217 transfer report on residential or farm property
  • Transfer tax of $4.50 per $500 of price, made up of $2.00 for New York State and $2.50 for Erie County, owed by the seller

On a $160,000 sale that rate works out to $1,440 in transfer tax. The original deed is recorded in the clerk's office and mailed back once indexing is verified, and a Notice of Sale or Transfer of Ownership form goes in with a residential deed.

Inside the city, the Department of Assessment and Taxation reviews every deed filed to update ownership records. Its tax office sends delinquent notices, helps owners set up court-ordered payment plans and runs an annual In Rem foreclosure auction, so a house with unpaid city taxes is worth sorting out before an offer is signed. Ask that office for a current balance, including sewer rent, before you close.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Buffalo house that has tenants living in it?
faqs.a: Yes. The buyer takes the house with the tenants in place, so ask the Rental Registration office whether your address holds a current Certificate of Rental Compliance. The city says a rental that fails inspection cannot operate as an income property, which makes a buyer ask about it early.

faqs.q: How much does Buffalo charge to register a rental house?
faqs.a: A new application is $100, and the annual fee is $50 for a single-unit dwelling or $100 for a two-unit dwelling. LLCs and corporations that own rentals must also file owner information at renewal.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax when I sell in Buffalo?
faqs.a: The seller pays. Erie County's clerk lists the combined rate as $4.50 per $500 of the sale price, with $2.00 going to the state and $2.50 to the county. A sale at $160,000 would owe $1,440.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to rent my Buffalo house by the night?
faqs.a: Yes. Buffalo requires a Short-Term Rental License for any stay shorter than six months. The license does not move with the house, so a buyer who wants to keep renting short term has to apply again.

faqs.q: Where is a Buffalo deed recorded?
faqs.a: At the Erie County Clerk's Office. The deed must be signed and notarized, and it is filed with the TP-584 and RP-5217 forms. The clerk mails the original back after recording.
